cohort: The study included 128 women in their first seven months after childbirth.
finding: Vaginal birth was associated with reduced pelvic floor muscle strength, while caesarean section had a protective effect; UI during pregnancy, previous pregnancies, and higher newborn weights predicted UI after childbirth; and AI prior to pregnancy was a risk factor for AI after childbirth.
mod_finding: Vaginal birth predisposes to the reduction of pelvic floor muscle strength, and caesarean section had a protective effect against its reduction.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from women in their first seven months after childbirth.
birth_weight: Newborn's weight was measured, with higher weights being associated with an increased likelihood of UI after childbirth.
